cards.title: Use the Facebook Ads Library to study live competitor creative
cards.summary: Find and reverse-engineer competitors' current Facebook ads by pulling them up and checking which creatives persist over weeks.
cards.use_when: Sourcing ad creative ideas and hooks for your store's paid social without relying on stale swipe files.

cards.title: Structure a 10-email launch sequence with three phases
cards.summary: Map a launch as email 1 (introduction), emails 2-7 (lessons, repurposed content, testimonials, FAQs), and emails 8-10 (triple close).
cards.use_when: Planning a product launch email sequence for a store drop, new offer or seasonal promotion.

cards.title: Choose launch pacing: aggressive, moderate or relaxed
cards.summary: Match the cadence of new sends and unopen resends to how urgently you need launch revenue.
cards.use_when: Scheduling the timeline of a product launch email sequence for a store.

cards.title: Resend launch emails to unopens with new subject and preview
cards.summary: Increase total reach of each launch email by resending to non-openers with a fresh subject line and preview text.
cards.use_when: Planning launch or promotional email sends for a store and wanting more subscribers to see existing copy.

cards.title: Write the triple close: three sales emails on closing day
cards.summary: Send three strong sales emails on the final day of a launch instead of one, timed across morning, afternoon and evening.
cards.use_when: Final day of a store launch or promotion when you want to capture last-chance buyers across time zones.

cards.title: Write quick-win lesson emails for the middle of a launch
cards.summary: Use teach-then-soft-CTA emails in the launch middle, capping each with a reminder that the product is for sale.
cards.use_when: Filling the middle days of a store launch sequence with value that keeps the audience engaged without unsubscribing.

cards.title: Repurpose existing content into a launch email
cards.summary: Turn prior videos, live events, reading lists or tutorials into a middle-of-launch email that drives clicks to your offer.
cards.use_when: Running a launch sequence and needing email content without writing new assets from scratch.

cards.title: Build testimonial and FAQ emails around objections
cards.summary: Use launch emails 2-7's success and FAQ slots to answer the specific objections blocking purchases.
cards.use_when: Filling launch sequence gaps with social proof and objection handling for a store offer.

cards.title: Use sentiment matching from reviews to mirror prospect language
cards.summary: Read five-star and one-star testimonials to capture the exact internal narrative prospects use to describe their problem.
cards.use_when: Writing store PDP, ad or email copy and needing the customer's actual words instead of brand wording.

cards.title: Lead prospects from their reality to the primary conversion goal
cards.summary: Account for the gap between the owner's expert context and the prospect's everyday perspective when writing any asset.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing why store copy about the transformation fails to land with prospects even though the product is good.

cards.title: Triple Close: Three Cart-Close Emails in One Day
cards.summary: Send three short cart-closing emails across morning, afternoon and evening of the final day instead of one or two.
cards.use_when: Planning the final day of a launch or sale campaign (cart close, promotion deadline, drop ending) and deciding how many closing emails to schedule.

cards.title: Late-Night Subject Lines: Short, Lowercase, No Punctuation
cards.summary: Use very short, casual, lowercase subject lines for late-evening sends and avoid periods that signal 'stop reading'.
cards.use_when: Writing subject lines for evening or final-day emails in a launch, flash sale or abandoned-cart sequence.

cards.title: Text-Only Emails to Stay Out of Promotions and Spam
cards.summary: Send plain-text emails without HTML templates or heavy images so promotions copy doesn't get filtered or clipped.
cards.use_when: Setting up any ecommerce email sequence — welcome, launch, or replenishment — where deliverability to the primary inbox matters.

cards.title: Write Email Sequences From an Outline Before Drafting
cards.summary: Decide the number of emails and their function first, then fill in subject, preview, story and content for each.
cards.use_when: Starting any ecommerce email campaign — launch, welcome, replenishment or abandoned-cart — and deciding where to begin.

cards.title: Seven-Email Welcome Series for New Subscribers
cards.summary: Send a daily seven-day welcome automation that delivers a video lesson and a short pitch while engagement is highest.
cards.use_when: Setting up an ecommerce welcome automation for new email signups, especially for a product that benefits from tutorials.

cards.title: Ecommerce Welcome Email #1: Discount Plus a Three-Column Best-Seller Block
cards.summary: Open with a welcome discount and a simple three-column best-sellers grid, then follow with product-tutorial emails.
cards.use_when: Drafting the first email of an ecommerce welcome sequence for a product-led store.

cards.title: Match Sales-Page Copy to Customer Awareness Stage
cards.summary: Set story length and proof density based on how aware the buyer is of their problem, the solution category, and your product.
cards.use_when: Writing a product sales page, long-form landing page or launch email and deciding how much story to tell before selling.

cards.title: Sales-Page Template and Section Order
cards.summary: Copy a fixed section order — hero, story, proof, price positioning, objections, FAQs, repeated CTAs — to prevent incoherent pages.
cards.use_when: Building a sales page, product landing page or long-form collection page and deciding section-by-section structure.

cards.title: Building a Cohesive Through-Line From Sub-Headers
cards.summary: Test sales-page cohesion by reading only the sub-headlines and checking whether they tell a complete story.
cards.use_when: Editing a sales page, landing page or launch sequence and deciding whether the sections connect.

cards.title: Sentiment Matching: Mine Reviews for Your Customer's Own Words
cards.summary: Read 5-star and 1-star reviews of competing or analogous products to learn the exact language customers use about the problem.
cards.use_when: Starting a product launch, PDP rewrite or ad campaign and needing customer language to write copy in.

cards.title: Positioning the Price: Offer Stack or Apples-to-Oranges Comparison
cards.summary: Break your offer into individual features with value assigned, or compare your price against the cost of alternatives.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to present pricing on a sales page, bundle page or checkout for high-ticket or multi-part offers.

cards.title: Plan the Email Count Before You Write the Sequence
cards.summary: Decide the number of emails in a launch or welcome sequence up front, then fill in the outline.
cards.use_when: Starting a launch or welcome sequence and planning how many sends are needed.

cards.title: Use Second-Person 'You' Copy and Drop Your Own Logic
cards.summary: Write in second person and reason with the customer's logic, not yours, since their background and framing differ from yours.
cards.use_when: Writing or editing email, PDP or ad copy where the copy favors the brand's reasoning over the buyer's.

cards.title: Choosing Email Software: Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, or Infusionsoft
cards.summary: Pick beginner, intermediate or enterprise email software based on list size and membership-site needs.
cards.use_when: Selecting an ESP for a growing ecommerce store and deciding when to migrate.

cards.title: Use Short Headlines to Carry a Story Across a Page
cards.summary: Write sales-page headlines that function as a sequence of mini-lines telling the reader's story in order.
cards.use_when: Writing the hero section and section headers of a product or launch sales page.

cards.title: Punctuation and Formatting Discipline in Subject Lines
cards.summary: Avoid punctuation that signals stopping and reserve periods for body copy, not the subject line.
cards.use_when: Reviewing subject lines in any ecommerce email campaign before launch.

cards.title: Start Writing Copy as Soon as Possible, Even by Hand
cards.summary: Get a first draft down quickly to avoid blank-page paralysis — outline first, then write fast.
cards.use_when: Failing to start a launch, welcome or PDP copy project because the scope feels overwhelming.

cards.title: The four-step Google Ads pipeline: retrieval, elimination, ranking, auction
cards.summary: Understanding Google's internal ad-serving sequence explains why relevance, not budget, drives placement.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing why Shopping or Search ads aren't showing, or deciding what to optimize first when a product campaign underperforms.

cards.title: Surface area scaling: duplicate products across pricing tiers to own the search page
cards.summary: Multiply one winning product into multiple listings differentiated by price tier so you occupy several ad slots at once.
cards.use_when: Product selection, merchandising and campaign structure decisions when a single hero SKU is already profitable and you want to grow without simply raising budget.

cards.title: Differentiate duplicate listings with image angles matched to customer avatars
cards.summary: Instead of one product shot per SKU, create lifestyle/angle variants so each listing speaks to a different buyer persona.
cards.use_when: PDP/landing page and Shopping feed creative decisions when a single image set makes every product look like everyone else's.

cards.title: Write relevant, readable Shopping feed titles from product attributes
cards.summary: Use accurate product type, audience, attributes and use cases to clarify search relevance.
cards.use_when: Writing Shopping feed titles for actual product variants; adapt separately for PDP titles and Search ad headlines.

cards.title: Set up a lean Performance Max campaign limited to Search and Shopping
cards.summary: Strip out Gmail, Display, Maps, Discover and YouTube placements in PMax to concentrate budget on high-intent surfaces.
cards.use_when: Campaign setup for an ecommerce account launching its main Google campaign, or auditing an existing PMax that is spending on low-intent placements.

cards.title: Don't set a tROAS target before the account has conversion history
cards.summary: Premature tROAS targets throttle scaling; the source waits months before adding one.
cards.use_when: Deciding when to apply target ROAS to a Performance Max or Shopping campaign on a new or growing ecommerce account.

cards.title: Consolidate campaigns instead of segmenting by product line
cards.summary: Contrary to popular advice to run many separated campaigns, the source argues one consolidated campaign outperforms segmented structures in ecommerce.
cards.use_when: Campaign architecture decisions when deciding how many Google campaigns to run per product category.

cards.title: Work the learning phase: 30 conversions in 30 days is the baseline, not a cap
cards.summary: Google's stated learning phase threshold is 30 conversions in 30 days, but aligned feeds can exit faster.
cards.use_when: Planning launch expectations and diagnosing persistent under-delivery after a new campaign or new ad account launch.

cards.title: Weekly optimisation cadence: tROAS, budget, negative keywords, product pruning
cards.summary: A tight weekly Google Ads review cycle beats constant tinkering; the source changes only a few levers each week.
cards.use_when: Setting up an ecommerce account's recurring Google Ads management routine.

cards.title: Use Google's intent-by-relevance CPC model to gauge paid search economics
cards.summary: Google's modern CPC is described by the source as the customer's purchasing intent multiplied by the advertiser's relevance.
cards.use_when: Evaluating keyword/bid economics and deciding whether a mid-relevance advertiser should compete on a high-intent query.

cards.title: Add a branded search campaign to defend your brand term cheaply
cards.summary: A separate brand campaign ensures your store appears first when shoppers search your name.
cards.use_when: Defensive campaign setup for an established ecommerce brand seeing competitors or review sites outrank its own name in search.

cards.title: Treat beta (experience penalty) as the long-term ranking lever
cards.summary: The source's ad score formula subtracts a penalty for poor post-click experience, and that penalty decreases with persistent quality and conversion history.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to invest alongside acquisition — site speed, delivery reliability, customer experience — to lower paid search costs over time.

cards.title: Build a broad keyword pool with Keyword Planner before writing feed copy
cards.summary: Mine real search terms in Keyword Planner and feed them into title/description templates to widen your query coverage.
cards.use_when: Paid search or Shopping feed title and description creation, and expansion of a keyword strategy.

cards.title: Prefer PVMs consolidations before adding new campaign types
cards.summary: Before introducing a new campaign type, confirm your current single campaign has genuinely plateaued.
cards.use_when: Scaling an ecommerce ad account when tempted to add campaign types to solve a performance plateau.

cards.title: Interview alignment: relevance across feed, landing page and price point
cards.summary: The algorithm scans the entire store surface as targeting data, so misaligned listings dilute delivery.
cards.use_when: Landing page and feed QA when diagnosing declining impressions, rising CPCs or low volume of conversions after a period of stability.

cards.title: Aim for high page position and read the clicks-per-position trade-off
cards.summary: Higher ranked positions capture disproportionately more click share, so ranking work is fundamentally a demand-capture play.
cards.use_when: Setting expectations for a Google campaign and prioritising rank/impression-share work over superficial creative prettiness.

cards.title: Google Ads is a demand-capture channel, not a fix for broken marketing
cards.summary: Treat Google Ads as a demand-capture engine that channels existing purchase intent, not as a rescue for weak product-market fit.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to launch or scale Google Ads for your store versus fixing offer, product and messaging first.

cards.title: Treat Google as four ad platforms in one
cards.summary: Plan Google as four distinct placements — search, shopping, YouTube and display — each covering a different intent level.
cards.use_when: Structuring a store's full Google Ads account and deciding which campaign types to build.

cards.title: Build a cold-customer magnet funnel across Google
cards.summary: Assemble top, middle and bottom-of-funnel Google campaigns so every awareness stage leads to a purchase path.
cards.use_when: Designing the full campaign architecture for an ecommerce store that wants to capture cold customers across Google.

cards.title: Scale at break-even using LTV-to-CAC, not front-end ROAS
cards.summary: Focus on break-even new-customer ROAS/CPA and lifetime value rather than chasing isolated high front-end ROAS.
cards.use_when: Setting bid targets and budgets for a store deciding how aggressively to acquire customers.

cards.title: Structure branded traffic separately before scaling
cards.summary: Isolate Branded Search and Branded Shopping from prospecting so Google doesn't waste budget converting people who already know you.
cards.use_when: Cleaning up campaign segmentation in a Google Ads account before increasing spend.

cards.title: The cold customer magnet funnel structure
cards.summary: A three-layer Google setup — demand generation, demand capture, conversion — covering all awareness stages.
cards.use_when: Designing the full Google campaign architecture for an ecommerce store.

cards.title: Know the role of each ecommerce Google campaign type
cards.summary: Assign campaign types to specific jobs — PMax and Shopping for capture, search for intent, YouTube for demand generation.
cards.use_when: Choosing which campaign types to launch for a store at its current scale and deciding which to prioritize.

cards.title: The three phases of ecommerce Google Ads growth
cards.summary: Sequence Google Ads growth — foundation/testing, then bidding and expansion, then scale — rather than launching everything at once.
cards.use_when: Deciding what to build first when launching or rebuilding a store's Google Ads account.

cards.title: Trust Google's automation but set guardrails
cards.summary: Let Google optimize broadly while controlling the points that matter, rather than micromanaging or abandoning control.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much manual control to keep over keywords, bidding and targeting in a store's Google Ads account.

cards.title: Scale as a process, not an event
cards.summary: Scale spend in steps with daily, weekly and monthly routines that maintain efficiency before adding budget.
cards.use_when: Managing an existing store's Google Ads account and deciding when and how much to increase spend.

cards.title: Cut poor SKUs and cap brand spend for efficiency
cards.summary: Improve Google Ads efficiency by concentrating on hero products and limiting branded campaign spend to a small share of budget.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a store's product-level ad spend and branded campaign budgets to eliminate waste.

cards.title: Expand beyond search and shopping with YouTube
cards.summary: Add YouTube and demand-gen campaigns to generate new search volume once native search demand is exhausted.
cards.use_when: Deciding when to move beyond search and shopping campaigns for a store hitting a growth ceiling.

cards.title: Test and iterate ads and landing pages continuously
cards.summary: Run split tests on search ad copy, product feeds and landing pages so you always have a control to beat.
cards.use_when: Setting up ongoing optimization for a store's Google Ads and PDP/landing pages.

cards.title: Make the offer the centerpiece of Google ads
cards.summary: Since Google shows your ad next to competitors, a stronger offer — shipping, BOGO, bundles — drives the click and conversion.
cards.use_when: Designing ad copy and promotions for a store competing in comparative Google search and shopping results.

cards.title: Diagnose weak performance via landing page congruence
cards.summary: When ads get clicks but no conversions, check session duration and ad-page congruence before blaming the ads.
cards.use_when: Troubleshooting a store's Google Ads where impressions and clicks are strong but conversions are low.

cards.title: Prioritize AOV over COGS cuts for scalable unit economics
cards.summary: Improve ad scalability mainly by increasing average order value and leveraging LTV, not by squeezing down COGS.
cards.use_when: Evaluating whether a store has the margin to run and scale Google Ads.

cards.title: Track the metrics that matter for ecommerce Google Ads
cards.summary: Monitor impression share, CPC, CTR, conversion rate and conversion count, plus average session duration, to steer campaigns.
cards.use_when: Building a reporting dashboard or weekly review for a store's Google Ads account.

cards.title: Diagnose Google Ads health in the right order
cards.summary: Use a fixed sequence of account-level metrics to find the real bottleneck before touching campaigns.
cards.use_when: Your Google Ads spend is rising but profit is flat, and you need to decide whether to fix creative, landing page, offer or campaign setup before scaling budget.

cards.title: Set up Shopify-to-Google Ads purchase conversion tracking
cards.summary: Configure enhanced conversions with purchase as the primary goal, then correctly order the remaining funnel events.
cards.use_when: You are launching Google Ads or your reported conversions do not match Shopify orders and you need trustworthy purchase data before scaling.

cards.title: Structure campaigns by funnel stage and start at the bottom
cards.summary: Split cold, mid-funnel and branded campaigns so cold and branded conversion data stay visible and separately attributable.
cards.use_when: You are planning a Google Ads account architecture or reworking an account where branded and non-branded results are blended and unreadable.

cards.title: Write Google ads from audience research, not keyword lists
cards.summary: Ground search ads, shopping titles and YouTube angles in the language and motivations of the person searching.
cards.use_when: You are writing search ad copy, shopping titles or a YouTube short for a cold audience and need angle and language direction.

cards.title: Let Shopping and PMax discover your converting keywords
cards.summary: Use broad-match Shopping/PMax search term reports as first-party keyword research rather than guessing keywords upfront.
cards.use_when: You need real, purchase-confirmed search phrases for search campaigns, shopping titles or landing page copy.

cards.title: Use manual keyword tools only for the first rung
cards.summary: Seed initial search campaigns with third-party keyword data, then hand research over to Google's conversion data.
cards.use_when: You have no conversion history and must launch a first search campaign or decide initial product title targets.

cards.title: Set bids and budgets from unit economics, not habit
cards.summary: Choose bidding strategies per campaign type and let your margins and KPIs define how much you can afford to bid and spend.
cards.use_when: You are setting bid strategy and daily budget for branded, shopping, PMax or cold campaigns.

cards.title: Enrol the four GMC add-ons
cards.summary: Turn on dynamic remarketing, customer reviews, product ratings and promotions in Merchant Center to lift CTR and enable remarketing.
cards.use_when: You are setting up or auditing Google Merchant Center before running Shopping, PMax or remarketing.

cards.title: Complete GMC business info and branding to survive review
cards.summary: Fill business details, verified store, logo/colour assets and social profiles accurately to protect account standing.
cards.use_when: You are onboarding a store to Merchant Center or your account has warnings and you want to reduce suspension risk.

cards.title: Lock shipping and returns as manual in GMC
cards.summary: Fix shipping and returns configuration inside Merchant Center so Shopify changes cannot desync policies and trigger suspension.
cards.use_when: You are configuring Merchant Center shipping/returns or your store changes shipping rates and you fear feed or policy mismatches.

cards.title: Audit feeds and fix 'needs attention' errors
cards.summary: Locate your primary feed and systematically clear product-level errors before scaling feed ads.
cards.use_when: You are diagnosing why feed ads underperform, or onboarding a store whose products are disapproved or warning-flagged.

cards.title: Build product titles with the 130–150 character formula
cards.summary: Frontload high-volume keywords and differentiators in feed titles, placing brand first or last depending on brand strength.
cards.use_when: You are rewriting Shopping/PMax feed titles to raise relevance and win more qualifying impressions.

cards.title: Write feed descriptions that survive policy review
cards.summary: Use the description for targeting and benefit copy, not promotions, and avoid website copy dumps.
cards.use_when: You are optimising feed descriptions for a store that simply imports Shopify product copy into Merchant Center.

cards.title: Choose feed images for context and standout
cards.summary: Test main images that show the product in use versus on plain backgrounds to improve Shopping ad click appeal.
cards.use_when: You are choosing or testing primary feed images for product pages and Shopping/PMax assets.

cards.title: Fill product identifiers, categories and attributes accurately
cards.summary: Use GTINs, product type, category and filtering attributes to remove performance-limiting warnings and increase discoverability.
cards.use_when: Your feed shows warnings about identifiers or missing attributes, or you want products to appear under Shopping filters.

cards.title: Never edit price or availability inside GMC
cards.summary: Change price, availability and sale price only at source so Google does not flag a website mismatch.
cards.use_when: You are updating product pricing or stock and deciding where to make the change.

cards.title: Earn the Shopping experience scorecard badge
cards.summary: Use Google's store quality scorecard to catch missing trust factors and differentiate listings with a trusted badge.
cards.use_when: You want Shopping listings to stand out against competitors and are looking for the highest-leverage remaining trust improvements.

cards.title: Run a weekly and monthly GMC maintenance rhythm
cards.summary: Keep Merchant Center healthy with recurring checks for feed errors, policy drift and promotion dates.
cards.use_when: You run feed campaigns continuously and need an operating routine that prevents gradual account decay or suspension.

cards.title: Reduce Merchant Center suspension risk deliberately
cards.summary: Treat suspension as the highest-cost ecommerce event and run the checklist that keeps feed, Shopping and PMax running.
cards.use_when: You are auditing an account for suspension risk or your store has received warnings, mismatches or policy flags.

cards.title: Product Feed Optimization Basics for Google Merchant Center
cards.summary: Keep feed titles, descriptions and images simple and accurate, sync availability automatically, and never edit sale price inside GMC.
cards.use_when: Optimizing your Google Merchant Center product feed so Shopping and PMax ads can serve correctly and convert.
